hypothesis: A multi-metric framework will reveal restoration quality differences that are not visible from PSNR/SSIM alone.
current_evidence: The final framework combines MSE, PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, CLIP, DINOv2, visual diagnostics, metric disagreement cases, and refined metric-region policy.

hypothesis: Pretrained models will behave differently across painting categories and damage types.
current_evidence: OpenCV Telea, LaMa, and Stable Diffusion were compared over 200 non-zero damage cases, with summaries by mask type and painting category.

hypothesis: Variation among multiple diffusion restoration candidates can act as a warning signal for generative restoration uncertainty.
current_evidence: Stable Diffusion was evaluated on a balanced 40-case subset using four seeds per case, producing image-space, LPIPS, CLIP/DINOv2, and combined uncertainty summaries.
